title: The filesystem: folders, extensions, shortcuts and search

videos.script: Everything a computer keeps is a file, and every file is in exactly one place. {{one}} That place is a path: a line down a tree from the root to the thing. A path is the only unambiguous way to name a file, and everything else is a nickname — a shortcut, a recent list, a search result. {{path}} Two ideas here do more work than the rest. The first is that an extension is a hint and not a fact. The letters after the last dot are a label anybody can change, and the commonest way a person is tricked into running a program is a document whose name ends in dot p d f dot e x e with the last part hidden from them. {{ext}} The second is that a name is the only thing a search has to work with. A folder of files called document, document two and final final is a folder you will search by opening things. {{name}} And we finish on dates, which is the one naming rule that pays for itself inside a week.
